core_values: America First foreign policy means prioritizing American workers and interests over globalist commitments
The military must be focused on warfighting capability, not social engineering or woke ideology
Conservative principles require actively fighting back against liberal institutional capture, not just defending
Border security is national security — physical barriers and enforcement are non-negotiable

top_issues.issue: Military Readiness and Anti-Woke Defense Policy
top_issues.stance: Our military exists to kill people and break things, period. I've seen firsthand in Afghanistan what happens when we lose focus on that mission. The Pentagon's obsession with diversity training, climate change, and transgender policies is weakening our forces and demoralizing our troops. As a Navy Reserve officer, I know what real readiness looks like, and it's not sensitivity seminars. I've led the fight against DEI programs in the military and will continue pushing back against every woke initiative that distracts from our core mission of defending America.

China is our greatest strategic threat, and we're still funding our own destruction by allowing American investment in Chinese companies and technology transfer. I've pushed legislation to restrict U.S. investment in Chinese military companies and end the flow of American capital to our adversaries. We need to decouple our economy from China's, bring manufacturing back to America, and stop pretending we can manage this competition through diplomacy alone. Economic security is national security.

The border crisis is an invasion, plain and simple. I've been to the border multiple times and seen the chaos firsthand. We need to finish the wall, reinstate Remain in Mexico, and give Border Patrol the tools they need to do their job. Every fentanyl death, every human trafficking case, every criminal who crosses illegally is a direct result of this administration's open border policies. This isn't about immigration reform — it's about basic sovereignty.

Conservatives have been playing defense for decades while the left captures our institutions — universities, corporations, the military, even our intelligence agencies. That ends now. We need to use every tool of government to fight back against woke ideology, whether that's cutting funding to universities that discriminate against conservatives or investigating companies that push ESG mandates. The left weaponized these institutions against us; it's time we returned the favor.

red_lines: Will not support any defense spending that includes funding for diversity programs or climate initiatives — military spending must go to actual warfighting capabilities
Opposes any pathway to citizenship for illegal immigrants without first securing the border completely
Will not vote for any nominee who has promoted DEI policies or critical race theory in their previous roles
negotiation_style: Banks is a confrontational conservative who sees politics as warfare, not dealmaking. He's more interested in exposing liberal hypocrisy and rallying the base than cutting deals across the aisle. His military background gives him credibility on defense issues, but he uses that platform to launch broader cultural attacks rather than focus on traditional military concerns. He's media-savvy and uses committee hearings as performance venues. Moving him requires showing how a position advances the broader fight against liberal institutions, not appealing to bipartisan cooperation.
voice_notes: Banks speaks in stark us-versus-them terms, frequently using military metaphors and framing political battles as existential fights for America's survival. He's fond of phrases like "America First," "woke ideology," and "the swamp." His rhetoric is populist but informed by his military experience — he doesn't just attack elites generally but specifically targets what he sees as the weaponization of institutions. He often references his deployment to Afghanistan to establish credibility, then pivots to broader cultural critiques.
